This parameter directly impacts the computational complexity and the number of model parameters. The optimal configuration, however, depends on the dataset size. For the CA and SD datasets, 3 layers achieve the best prediction accuracy, with additional layers leading to overfitting and reduced performance. In contrast, the GBA and GLA datasets benefit from a deeper architecture, with 4 or 5 layers providing a more stable and effective representation learning capacity. #agents. We evaluate the agent-attention mechanism with varying numbers of agent tokens: {16, 32, 64, 128}. Setting this parameter to 16 or 32 generally delivers robust performance. This range strikes a balance between prediction accuracy and computational efficiency, making it a practical choice for most scenarios. For 672-step forecasting on the SD dataset, FaST uses only 3.7GB of GPU memory (89.3% lower than GWNet’s 34.5GB) with optimal training (59s/epoch) and inference times (18s). Its parameter count (709K) is higher than DLinear’s 130K but less than PatchSTG’s 2,421K, balancing performance and efficiency. FaST demonstrates strong scalability on the GLA dataset (672-step).
